title: Codex MCP file-change receipt v1 (inline only)
$comment: Authoritative candidate contract for the value of CallToolResult._meta['codex/fileChanges']. Acceptance requires BOTH this JSON Schema and x-codex-validation. No artifact/resource references in v1. No producer-supplied call, turn, thread or environment IDs.

x-codex-validation.attachmentEncoding: UTF-8 compact JSON; no insignificant whitespace; Unicode unescaped except JSON-required escaping. Measure the decoded attachment reserialized this way, not the original transport's whitespace.
rules: Metadata describes producer-reported captured effects, not host-verified filesystem truth, approval, permission, or replay authority.

outcome preview: no publication attempted. outcome applied: requested file publication completed, possibly a no-op. outcome notApplied: positively known no publication. outcome partial: positively known published effects but incomplete requested publication; no unresolved effects. outcome unknown: publication is unresolved anywhere, even when some individual effects are known.

publication applied: before/after are actual captured endpoints of this file's published transition, not a promise that the overall request succeeded. publication preview: before is captured input and after is prospective, not proof of a write. Path-only entries carry intended path identity and no existence/content assertions.
A null before/after snapshot means absence, never unknown. Unknown content or publication MUST use pathOnly, not fabricated hashes or a planned after snapshot labeled applied.

URI must be an absolute file URI with absolute path, no userinfo/query/fragment, valid percent escapes, no raw control characters. Compare the producer's URI strings without resolving paths or symlinks. URI identity is scoped to the originating MCP binding; never infer host-local identity from file:// or localhost.

For modify, before.uri equals after.uri (or beforeUri equals afterUri). For rename, these strings differ. Before URIs must be unique among listed records; after URIs must be unique among listed records. A producer coalesces its own repeated writes to one captured transition per logical file; cross-file swaps are allowed. Do not merge unrelated filesystem state into the receipt.

Snapshot sha256 is lowercase SHA-256 of original bytes, without text/EOL normalization. bytes is that original byte length. Consumer validates representation, not the truth of an unavailable snapshot.

Text entries must describe UTF-8 text and provide a complete single-file unified diff, with ---/+++ headers and complete hunks when content changes. Preserve no-final-newline markers. Diff headers never determine routing/path identity. No raw git binary patches, multiple-file patches, or truncated hunks.

Empty unifiedDiff is allowed only for empty-file creation/deletion or content-preserving rename. A modify with identical before/after hash and byte length is a no-op and is omitted, not a fake edit row. Pure mode/permission changes are outside v1; keep them in ordinary model-visible output.

Summary binary means content classified as binary; nonUtf8 means text cannot be represented losslessly in this UTF-8 channel; oversized means the complete text diff or inline attachment budget prevented inclusion. Do not put a partial diff or source excerpt into summary. Unknown hash/content is not a summary: use pathOnly with publication unknown.

omittedFiles is the exact count of additional file records deliberately excluded for inline bounds, not a count of writes. Their publication categories must obey the global outcome. Never truncate silently. If the count cannot be determined, omit the optional presentation attachment rather than fabricate completeness.

outcome applied with files=[] and omittedFiles=0 is a proven no-op. preview with the same empty shape is a no-op preview. unknown with empty files does NOT assert that no writes occurred; paths/effects may be unavailable. partial requires at least one listed applied transition or omittedFiles>0.

Reject malformed/over-limit/unsupported metadata as one presentation attachment. Preserve the original MCP success/failure and ordinary model-facing result; never retry an edit to repair presentation. Unknown versions are not v1 and must not be interpreted using this schema.

Host assigns source binding, thread/turn/nested-call identity and outer-call grouping. Persist only a bounded normalized human-transcript attachment; exclude source bytes from model/Guardian history, compaction, Code Mode results, token estimates, and telemetry.

The model-visible result must retain outcome, counts, assurances, failures and recovery information. Publication failures use isError:true CallToolResult with the full existing fault/hint/retryability plus private receipt; protocol/selection/validation errors need not migrate. This changes rejected-promise behavior to a resolved error result and must be explicit to callers.

v1 offers no full-diff inspection route for omitted/summary-only changes. Show that limitation explicitly; do not fetch URIs, open paths, emit fake native apply_patch approvals/events, or silently substitute current worktree content. Resource transport requires a later separately agreed version.
